To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

miRNA-155 is upregulated in proliferative lupes nephritis and is involved in the development of proliferative LN through the regulation of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) and that the expression of miR-155 in proliferative LN is associated with disease activity and the degree of renal injury.

the miR-200 family and miR-34a are up-regulated in LN, and miR-200c and miR-29a target the 3′ untranslated region of the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) mRNA and down-regulate the expression of HER2 in human glomerular mesangial cells.
miRNAs are important regulators of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) and its downstream pathways in proliferative LN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the roles of miRNAs and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) in proliferative LN.
the role of miRNAs in LN,
the role of miRNA-21 in the pathogenesis of LN and the potential role of miRNA in the treatment of LN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miRNAs are not the only players in the regulation of the immune system.
the use of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) in LN has not been well studied and the results are not conclusive.
the miRNA-34 family is a key regulator of cell proliferation and apoptosis, which may be involved in the pathogenesis and progression of human proliferative LN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miR-155 and miR-21 are up-regulated in proliferative LN and may be involved in the pathogenesis of proliferative LN through the regulation of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2).
miR-155 and miR-142-3p are involved in the development of proliferative LN.
the expression of miRNA 155, 21, and 146a are upregulated in the renal tissue of patients with LN, and that these microRNAs may be important in the development of proliferative LN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
miR-21 is a critical regulator of podocyte function, and its dysregulation is associated with podocyte injury in proliferative LN.

we identified a set of miRNAs that are differentially regulated in the renal cortex of patients with proliferative LN and that we identified the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) as a potential target for miR-146b-3p.
miRNAs play a role in the pathogenesis of LN, and that miRNA profiling can be used to predict disease outcome in patients with proliferative LN.
